_about.purpose: Versioned Algolia index configuration, pushed by scripts/2-index.js. Settings are never edited in the dashboard: the configuration is part of the codebase, it gets reviewed in diffs, and a dashboard-only change is a change nobody can trace (CLAUDE.md §5).
contract_for_2-index.js: Push `settings` verbatim to the primary index as the setSettings payload. It contains only real Algolia setting keys — nothing here needs filtering.

Derive the primary's `replicas` array from the `replicas` list below: each entry becomes `virtual(<indexName>_<suffix>)` for type `virtual`, or `<indexName>_<suffix>` for type `standard`. It is deliberately absent from `settings` so the replica list has exactly one source of truth.
Set the primary settings including the derived `replicas` FIRST, then push each replica's own `settings`. Algolia rejects settings on a replica that does not exist yet.
Keys prefixed with `_` are documentation and must never be sent to Algolia.
`_geoloc` needs no declaration — Algolia indexes it for geo search automatically.

not_implementable_as_specified.distance_replica: CLAUDE.md §5 lists a `distance` virtual replica. A replica cannot sort by distance: a replica's order comes from stored attributes, and distance depends on the user's position at query time. Nothing to store, nothing to pre-sort. Distance ordering is produced instead by sending `aroundLatLng` to the primary index, where the `geo` ranking criterion applies — which is exactly what the discovery parameter set does. The sort control therefore offers the primary index as its geo-aware default plus the three replicas below, and no `distance` replica is created. Note this rules out sorting by a stored distance, NOT a standard replica whose `ranking` places `geo` first — that is implementable and is one of the two candidate fixes for test-queries.md G3.

missing_from_the_repo_layout.synonyms: Persona 1 requires 'synonyms and alternative spellings' (CLAUDE.md §2), and test-queries.md K12 `pappas brothers` cannot pass without one — the edit distance from `Bros.` to `brothers` is 3, beyond any typo setting. Synonyms are a separate Algolia resource, not an index setting, so they do not belong in this file and CLAUDE.md §6 lists no file for them. They need `scripts/synonyms.json`, pushed by 2-index.js alongside these settings, for the same reason settings live in the repo: a dashboard-only synonym is untraceable.

_rationale.searchableAttributes: Attribute order is the main lever for persona 1: a query matching a restaurant name must beat a query matching a cuisine or a neighborhood, always. `unordered(name)` because word position inside a restaurant name carries no meaning. `location_label` and `market_state` are absent on purpose — the first duplicates neighborhood and city, the second is misleading (only 922 of 2,897 derived values are actual US state names). Two attributes were REMOVED after measurement. `chain_name` (2026-09-03): provably redundant, since all 722 chained records have a name beginning with their chain_name, 0 exceptions; being searchable it produced a whole-attribute exact match for every member of a chain whose base name equalled the query, which is what made test-queries.md A2 fail. `address` (2026-09-03): no stated pain requires street search (CLAUDE.md §1 puts unmotivated features out of scope), and it injected measurable noise into name and cuisine queries through typo-plus-prefix matching on street names — `kaya` returned 27 Waikiki restaurants on Kalakaua Avenue out of 67 hits, `thai` returned 31 restaurants on Third Street or Third Avenue out of 76, and `Cafe 21` returned 5 spurious hits on top of the 2 real ones. Removing it changed no case status but cut those tails: kaya 67 to 40, thai 76 to 45, union 57 to 42, tien 47 to 38, Cafe 21 7 to 2. It also moved O3 from 1 hit to 10, because the leak is not address but removeWordsIfNoResults — with word removal disabled, all four out-of-corpus queries return 0.
_rationale.attributesForFaceting: `searchable(cuisine)` because 37 primary values need a searchable facet list rather than a scroll. `cuisine_tags` is the second-level refinement that makes the American merge defensible — without it, one facet value covers 35% of the corpus with no way to narrow. `filterOnly(is_chain)` because nobody browses a boolean, but the UI may need to scope to chains. The three place facets were made searchable on 2026-09-03, after the UI called searchForFacetValues on them and the API refused outright: Cannot search in `city` attribute. Cardinality is why they need it rather than a longer `showMore` list — 916 distinct cities and 1,062 distinct neighborhoods against a `limit` of 6. No amount of scrolling reaches a named city, which is exactly what persona 2 does when browsing by place. `market` is included at only 51 values because it is an opaque label at inconsistent granularity (CLAUDE.md §3): a user looking for Fort Worth cannot guess it lives under `Dallas - Fort Worth`, so typing beats scanning. The flag enables facet-value search only: it does not add the attribute to `searchableAttributes`, so it cannot affect matching or ranking. Spot-checked rather than assumed — the five hit counts recorded for the `address` removal (kaya 40, thai 45, Cafe 21 2, union 42, tien 38) are unchanged, A2 still ranks 117067 first, A1 still ranks 95884 and 105424 above 30385, and G3 still returns Denver first from Denver.
_rationale.ranking:
Declared explicitly, because the order is a consequential choice and an implicit default is invisible in a diff. The value is Algolia's default order, with `geo` second, and that is a decision rather than an inherited default. 

`geo` outranks `exact` on purpose: in a reservation product the dominant intent signal is proximity. A diner is choosing somewhere to eat, so the near restaurant matching the query is usually the one wanted, and a diner who does want a specific restaurant in another city names that city. That fallback was measured, not assumed: 10 city-qualified queries from Denver each return exactly one hit at rank 1, because Algolia requires all query words to match whenever the full query has results, so `geo` never reorders them. See test-queries.md A1, A2 and A6, which are `accepted` on this basis and record the ten queries. 

The cost is recorded on those cases: from Denver, `prime` puts 117067 `Prime` at rank 14 of 49 behind `Ocean Prime - Denver`, `union` puts 116815 at rank 25 of 42 behind `Workshop at UNION`, and `bistro` puts 100624 at rank 198 of 208 behind Denver bistros. Do not 'fix' these by reordering `ranking` without reading those three cases first. 

Two departures were measured on 2026-09-04 and deliberately NOT applied. Promoting `exact` above `geo` recovers A1, A2 and A6 and was rejected because it inverts the intent model above. Demoting `attribute` below `custom` makes a category query lead with the best-rated nearby restaurant rather than the one carrying the category in its name — `steakhouse` from Denver leads with Morton's The Steakhouse (4.2) rather than Guard & Grace (4.7), `french` from Midtown West with French Roast Bar & Bistro (4.1) rather than Le Bernardin (4.7) — and is being addressed with a query rule instead, so the ranking formula stays Algolia's default. Both measurements are in test-queries.md and DECISIONS.md.
_rationale.customRanking: `desc(popularity_score)` before `desc(reviews_count)`. popularity_score is a Bayesian average, not raw stars: 21 records hold a 5.0 and 18 of those have fewer than 50 reviews, so ranking on `desc(stars_count)` would fill the first screen from that pool. The `reviews_count` tie-break separates records whose smoothed scores collide.
_rationale.typoTolerance: Thresholds carried over from §5. They are a measured compromise, not a default: 59 pairs of distinct restaurant names sit at edit distance 1, so tolerance can turn an exact known-item query into the wrong restaurant, while 36 names fall under the 4-character floor and get no tolerance at all. Do not move these without a test-queries.md case naming the pair the change fixes and the pair it puts at risk.
_rationale.disableTypoToleranceOnWords: Deliberately empty. This is the intended remedy for test-queries.md A3/A4 — `naya` (148411) against `kaya` (79378), both 4-character names in Pittsburgh, one character apart, so neither the typo floor nor geo separates them. It is left unset because the case has not been run yet: pre-tuning a setting to make a test pass before observing the failure is exactly what CLAUDE.md §8 forbids.
_rationale.queryType: `prefixLast` — the last word is a prefix, earlier words must match fully. Required by search-as-you-type, where the user is still typing: `melting po` must reach The Melting Pot. `prefixAll` would make every word a prefix and let `rye` match `Ryeland`, which directly harms A1.
_rationale.removeWordsIfNoResults: `lastWords` as specified, but flagged: test-queries.md O2 shows it actively harming. `olive garden` is absent from the corpus, and dropping the last word leaves `olive`, which matches six unrelated restaurants presented as answers. O3 `shake shack` is safe under the same setting because `shake` matches nothing. The same setting is therefore harmful on one query and harmless on another, which is why `allOptional` gets evaluated against those two cases rather than chosen by preference.
_rationale.ignorePlurals: Set to false, and the reason is measured rather than reasoned. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-04 as a query-time override, exhaustively: it buys **three zero-result queries and nothing else** — `breweries` 0 to 9 hits, `wineries` 0 to 10, `eateries` 0 to 11, `bakeries` 1 to 3, all the `-y`/`-ies` class at edit distance 3, beyond minWordSizefor2Typos. It costs **15 known-item regressions** across all 4,979 distinct names under the real geo parameters: `Basil's` returns Sweet Basil, `Grace's` Guard & Grace, `Oceans` Ocean Prime - Denver, `Latitudes` Latitude 41. The mechanism is the point — no hit count moves; rivals go from typo=1 to typo=0 and join the exact name in one bucket, where `geo` settles the tie five criteria before `exact`. Without geo the same sweep shows 2 regressions, so this is the geo decision's blast radius, not an independent setting. Half the damage is possessives: the apostrophe is dropped and the plural dictionary folds the possessive s into the stem. An earlier note credited typo tolerance with absorbing plurals; the actual neutraliser is rules.json — `steakhouses` and `italians` fire their category rule via `alternatives: true` either way. Kept false; the four `-ies` words belong in the synonyms.json K12 already needs.
_rationale.removeStopWords: Set to false, measured rather than reasoned. MEASURED 2026-09-03 with queryLanguages ["en"]: turning it on regresses the sharpest case in the corpus — `the smith` goes from 4 hits to 16 and 19258 `The Smith - East Village` falls out of the top 3 entirely, displaced by `Smithfields` and `Butera's Restaurant of Smithtown`. It adds tail noise elsewhere (`in the raw` 1 to 2 hits, `the capital grille` 11 to 12) and leaves `left bank`, `da umberto` and `the melting pot` unchanged. It buys nothing: an earlier note claimed it would help test-queries.md O4 by removing the matchable token `in`, but with word removal disabled `sushi in tokyo` already returns 0, so `in` was never the cause.
_rationale.attributesToHighlight: Highlighting is load-bearing rather than decorative here: with typo tolerance active, the user needs to see *why* a result matched. A query for `naya` returning `Kaya` is only comprehensible if the matched characters are marked.
_rationale.numericAttributesForFiltering: Restricted to the three attributes any journey actually filters on. popularity_score is absent on purpose — it is a ranking signal, never a user-facing filter, and exposing it invites filtering on a number the user cannot interpret.
_rationale.concatenated_queries: test-queries.md K13–K16 (`ilforno`, `leftbank`, `roaringfork`, `montblanc`) are not addressed by any setting in this file. Algolia's `decompoundedAttributes` covers German, Dutch, Finnish, Norwegian and Swedish, not English, so it does not apply. Whether the engine's built-in word splitting and concatenation is enough for these four names is an empirical question those cases exist to answer; if it is not, the fix is synonyms, not a setting.
_rationale.thresholds: minWordSizefor1Typo, minWordSizefor2Typos and allowTyposOnNumericTokens are the numeric half of the typoTolerance decision above. allowTyposOnNumericTokens is false because 257 names contain a digit — 31141 `12 Baltimore`, 92827 `53 by the Sea`, 90436 `247 Craven` — and a tolerated digit typo turns one address or house number into another.
_rationale.maxValuesPerFacet: Left at the Algolia default of 100, declared explicitly so it appears in a diff. It is a real ceiling here: `neighborhood` and `city` both exceed 100 distinct values, so a facet list on either is truncated. Acceptable because neither is browsed as a flat list — city is reached through `market`, and neighborhood only ever appears scoped to a city.
_rationale.paginationLimitedTo: Left at the default of 1000. No journey pages past the first few screens, and lowering it would break nothing while raising it costs performance for pages nobody reaches.
_rationale.exactOnSingleWordQuery: Declared at Algolia’s default value because the choice is measured, not inherited. `attribute` grants the exact criterion only when a single-word query equals the whole attribute value; `word` grants it when the query matches any whole word in the attribute. They are in direct opposition and no setting provides both. Measured at query time on 2026-09-03: `word` fixes test-queries.md G2 (all four Nobu score exact=1 while Nobuo, matched only as a prefix, scores 0) and breaks A2, A7 and A8 (`prime` returns Bohanan’s, `bistro` returns Costa Brava, `babylon` returns Babylon Turkish). Net −2, so `attribute` is kept — it serves three cases against one, and “the query is the whole name” is the stronger known-item signal.
_rationale.languages: `indexLanguages` and `queryLanguages` are both pinned to ["en"]. This is a prerequisite, not a preference: `ignorePlurals` and `removeStopWords` are dictionary-driven, and with no language declared they resolve against every supported language, which widens the plural and stop-word sets far beyond anything this corpus needs. Declaring English narrows both to the only language present (`country` is constant US across all 5,000 records) and makes the dictionary the engine consults reviewable rather than implicit. Measured on 2026-09-03 across 11 representative queries — thai, sushi, steakhouse, prime, bistro, rye, naya, kaya, nobu, pappas brothers, melting pott — the declaration alone changes nothing; it exists so the two settings below rest on a stated basis.

replicas.label: Top rated
replicas.rationale: Sorts on popularity_score, not stars_count. A raw-rating sort was rejected: 154318 `Ellen's Cafe` holds a 5.0 on a single review, and 18 of the 21 five-star records have fewer than 50 reviews, so `desc(stars_count)` would hand the first page to the thinnest evidence in the corpus under a label the user reads as a quality guarantee. The Bayesian average is what makes the label honest. Distinct from the primary because here popularity is applied as the sort criterion rather than as a tie-break after text relevance.

replicas.label: Price: low to high
replicas.rationale: price_tier is derived from the price_range label, never from the JSON price int, which contradicts it on 220 records. Only 3 tiers exist, so popularity_score does the real ordering inside each tier — without that second criterion a third of the corpus would be returned in arbitrary order.

replicas.label: Price: high to low
replicas.rationale: Mirror of price_asc. Kept as a separate replica rather than a UI reversal because virtual replicas cannot be read backwards.
